verdict.tagline: A sprawling sandbox marred by technical stutters and storefront pressure.
for_you_if: you want to construct custom fortresses
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates without stutters
you play on multiplayer servers with cheaters
you want to avoid expensive microtransactions

claims.claim: Reviewers note that building from the character perspective can be difficult at times.

citations.review_text:
It's just good ol regular fun, especially with friends. Exploring the world, maiming enemies, building your own fortress...
I played the game earlier on Xbox and the enchanced edition shows noticeable change, especially in the graphics departament.
The construction mode should provide more tools though, building from the character perspective can be a handful at times.

The "Enhanced" graphics really push this game into a great experience.   Just stopping and looking at the shadows, and water dynamics are amazing.  Highly recommend just for the visuals alone.  I normally am not a game person when it comes to building things due to the difficulties in doing so... however this makes it easy to grasp quickly on and keeps me interested on what can be done creatively.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat as feeling clunky, sluggish, or floaty.

citations.review_text:
Conan Exiles is a survival crafting game that can be played either solo or multiplayer on a server. Set in the Conan universe there is an emphasize on being "savage" and living in a harsh world. You'll be gathering resources, base building, crafting, fighting and exploring.

Ultimately I wanted to like this game but ended up bouncing off. I actually really like the aesthetic and world they have presented here, one where creatures are dangerous and vile, and people are even worse. Not only do the horrible enemies you take down engage in slavery and cannibalism, but you can too! Its a cruel world and you need to be cruel to survive. 

The problem is gameplay though. Combat is not great. feeling clunky to me. Crafting progression also felt off to me, where you seem to make big progress all around the "noob" river in the beginning, but then need to travel through fairly empty and not very interesting land to look for ways to advance. Things like magic are pretty hidden and not very obvious which isn't a bad thing by itself, but unfortunately exploring is not very interesting. The world feels like an old MMO, with large open spaces with enemies just kind of standing around and no real level design to speak off. So there is this tension, where there are resources you want to find, like characters that give you abilities, new metals, and even stories, but actually going through the world is a chore. There are things worth finding but the act of finding them sucks. 

The balance also feels off. While you can can edit XP rates, combat difficulty, resource requirements and so on, I strongly feel that it shouldn't be up to me to figure out how to make the game fun. Even the official servers do not use the default settings. My complaint isn't that you can edit these things, but rather that the suggested defaults are not really fun and you will want to tinker with them if you actually intend to play.

Overall I do think I will try to return to this game in the future, an…

I found the combat overall to feel pretty janky.  I found myself either dominating an enemy or being dominated by an enemy due to aspects of the game that were outside of my control.  There didn't seem to be any satisfying gameplay here.  It was just researching higher tier knowledge, so you can build higher tier crafting benches, so you craft higher tier armor/weapons, so you can fight higher tier monsters that are even more janky than the last tier of monsters.

Controller support works pretty well despite my not liking the game.  I found myself picking up the mouse a few times in menus and inventory management, but gameplay seems just as functional on gamepad as on mouse and keyboard.

I've only played for 8 hours and i am completely addicted. By the time i managed to pull myself away it was 2am. I can't wait to get back home and run around trying to survive. 

I don't know if this is the gold standard for this genre but it has me locked in and if there are better games i welcome  any recommendations. The Reasons i like this game are 

Stability: Games stable, well optimized, not running into any issues on my rinky dink 2070. Yea its chugging but still running with the highest settings while I have youtube videos playing in the background. Incredible. 

The Combat: It is a little sluggish but its paced well enough without being frustrating. With needs to manage stamina and how much each weapon consumes with needing to back away and recover or time your swings REALLY reminds me of Darksouls. Old school Darksouls without the fluidity that saturates the genre now. Dodging and sidestepping is very responsive and is what has saved me most of the time.   

Climbing: You can climb on everything breath of the wild style. It could use some tweaking but it works. Miscalculating the height of a climb only to fall down and shatter both your kneecaps is more punishing though because unlike in the mentioned game, in this one you lose everything you were carrying. WHICH YOU CAN EDIT, but like everything else the pain I endure is self inflicted so I leave that feature on. 

Nudity: You can turn it on or off, The gooner that is me appreciates the option.

There is a magic system I have not been able to get to yet because while exploring i was hit by a massive sandstorm that ate away my health, I died & lost everything, decided that I need to make base building my first priority, so i have been doing that for the 8 hours and fulfilling the "tasks" the game gives you in order to level up and assign attribute points. They occur with alarming unpredictability, because in the 8 hours I was on I had to fend off atleast 3 of them. 

The Ai & NPC system, I forget what the…

Skip it.  Don't ever be fooled by the "Enhanced" label or the Unreal Engine 5 upgrade. This game is a visual and mechanical relic of the mid-2010s that fails to meet 2026 standards.  It looks very average in 4K even with everything cranked to ULTRA with DLAA.

The game already set a low bar in terms of quality and porting the old code to UE5 doesn't fix old, low-quality character models and stiff animations. High-end lighting just makes the dated, plastic-looking assets stand out even more more.

Combat feels floaty, unresponsive, and imprecise.

The UI/UX is an archaic mess of clunky inventory menus that turns simple tasks into chores. 

This game is NOT cheap and we shouldn't accept it.

No real plot or interesting story, just some checklists (journeys), notes, mostly empty big map with POI, dungeons and other repetitive stuff. Crafting system is bloated with components and materials. Default grind amount is ridiculous, so if you do not want to work as full time in-game miner or lumberjack - you need to play on custom server. Default damage balance is the same as grind - you can not kill anything and all kills you. The only way to make this game playable is to create custom local server and manually tweak grind, hunger, damage, xp gain, so you will at least have realistic experience with no need to do second job in game. Dune is better in this context and at least has some story (unfinished yet).

Graphics is decent, framerate is smooth regardless the fact it is UE game. Combat is clunky and cringe, like in some cheap online game from 2010. Unique slave gathering mechanic, but I dont like it, because it is better to get thralls by releasing them from slavers or by hiring at the bar from the moral RPG perspective. A lot of crafting possibilities, but many of them are hidden behind paywall and game constantly remainds you that. Also it is using FOMO manipulation in its in-game store to make you spend more money for cosmetics.

After so many years of development from my perspective as new player it is good foundation for the game, but not really interesting game. Buy only on sale and if you like sandbox gameplay where you need to figure out how to entertain yourself.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the default game settings require an excessive amount of grind for materials and crafting.

citations.review_text:
Miserable jankfest, avoid.

The default settings are set to what I can only describe as a "korean MMO sweatshop." Everything is prohibitively expensive, takes far too long to make, and provides little benefit. This can be mitigated by adjusting the settings, but all that does is remove the grind, rather than create an engaging experience. There is also no fast travel system (at least not immediately, which is when it should be available), so gathering these materials incurs endless, boring treks back and forth.
Thrall system is impressively barebones. Instead of having workers that can help you around the base (mine resources, build, defend) they effectively function as "slottable upgrades" for various crafting stations around the base - you are still supposed to do everything, they just give you a processing boost. The system somehow manages to be even more dehumanizing than the slavery it portrays. For fighting, you just get a party that you can not control in any meaningful capacity (or at least the option to do so was not presented), so you are just always at the risk of the party doing nothing or suiciding against a random tough enemy. Games like soulmask and palworld do more with similar systems.
Combat is frustrating. There is no way to control the distance of engagement as rolling covers the grand distance of a millimeter for like a 5th of your stamina bar. Enemies can easily overwhelm you, and even if you have a party of thralls with you, enemies can just focus and delete you with a few combos.
Building can only be described as torture. There is no dedicated "build mode," so all the pieces must be placed, one by one, from the player's view. There does not seem to be any grid snapping for furniture and the like. Pieces routinely orient themselves in the one incorrect direction, or disallow placement because something is just a little bit too close for its comfort. Fixing things in place is basically impossible if the game refuses to cooperate. Creative …

Score: 8.5/10

Conan Exiles is a large-scale open-world survival game set in the brutal universe created by Robert E. Howard. Players begin as exiles left to die in a harsh wasteland and gradually build settlements, gather followers, conquer dungeons, and carve out their own place in the world.

What it does well

✅ Outstanding Base Building

Building is one of the game's strongest features.
Players can create anything from simple huts to enormous fortresses and cities.

✅ Rich World Design

The Exiled Lands are filled with deserts, jungles, mountains, ruins, and hidden secrets.
Exploration is consistently rewarding.

✅ Thrall System

Capturing and recruiting NPCs adds depth to progression.
Followers can assist with crafting, combat, and defending your settlements.

✅ Strong Sense of Progression

Starting with stone tools and eventually commanding powerful warriors and legendary equipment feels satisfying.

✅ Dungeon and Boss Content

Numerous dungeons, world bosses, and legendary creatures provide meaningful endgame goals.
Weaknesses

❌ Can Be Grindy

Gathering resources for large projects requires significant time investment.

❌ Occasional Bugs

Players may encounter AI issues, physics glitches, or server-related problems.

❌ PvP Can Be Harsh

On competitive servers, losing a base can represent many hours of work.
Who will enjoy it?

You'll probably enjoy it if you like:

Survival games
Base building
Open-world exploration
Fantasy settings
Character progression
Multiplayer communities
Standout Features
Extensive building system
Thrall recruitment mechanics
Large open world
Mounts and companions
Dungeons and world bosses
Clan-based multiplayer
Verdict

Conan Exiles offers a compelling blend of survival, exploration, and conquest. The freedom to build impressive settlements, recruit loyal followers, and venture into dangerous lands creates a strong sense of adventure and achievement. While it can demand a considerable time investment, players who enjoy long-term pro…

claims.claim: Reviewers experience motion sickness while playing.

citations.review_text:
Co-op worked, didn't crash for me. It does give me motion sickness, I wish it had an isometric view. 
You can enter god mode and build stuff that way like a sims 4 game, makes it less nauseating. 
It's nice having all the pets and cooking recipes. Dancing ladies with big boobies makes for nice background in the castle. I think there are dudes as well, would be nice if you could hire them in a less violent way, but in god mode you can cheat and spawn workers instead of beating and enslaving them. 
There is supposedly some story to this game, but we finished fairly quickly and I can't remember it. 
 Wish we had a Game of Thrones game like this or BG3.

I have not tried the PVP only private servers. Seems to be a hackers dream and lots of shady tactics that the devs don't seem to care about so don't sink any meaningful amounts of money and time into this game.
I tried all the options, but to no avail.  This game made me so motion sick I filled up a bucket.

cohorts.summary: Mid game players praise the building mechanics while reporting performance drops and restrictive co-op tethering.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the Unreal Engine 5 upgrade causes noticeable stutters and performance drops regardless of high system specifications.

citations.review_text: Conan Exiles Enhanced is a great survival game for players who enjoy exploration, crafting, combat, and building. The Enhanced version gives the game a major visual upgrade through Unreal Engine 5, making the world, characters, armor, buildings, lighting, and environments look much better than before The biggest downside is that Conan Exiles Enhanced still has some technical issues. Players have reported server performance problems, lag, and occasional mod compatibility issues, although Funcom has continued releasing patches and improvements.

Conan Exiles is my favorite survival and craft game, but I cannot recommended it.

It is completely random on whether or not the game will run well, not just between systems, but day to day. Before Enhanced edition it ran at a smooth 90 FPS for me. Afterward, it now runs at 140 fps, but stutters every ten seconds with frame drops all the way down to 32. I've lowered the graphics to their base level, increased shader cache space, and capped the frame rate to no avail. I've tried every tweak under the sun, updated my drivers, and performed numerous restarts and clean installs.

On the last clean install, my controller no longer works. The UI flickers constantly between mouse and keyboard and controller inputs, making both unusable.

You will troubleshoot this game, with zero mods, almost as often as you play it unless you're just very lucky.

An excellent game to start in 2026.  The Enhanced Edition has done wonders for Conan Exiles to make it relevant again.  I had skipped it because, well frankly, by the time I noticed it, it looked far too dated for me.

Now that it has the UE5 treatment (the good and the bad) it's a very viable game in 2026!
If you've played the likes of Valheim or Enshrouded, it's like that but much more mature.
This is not a family game, and I love that about it!

It's also a perfect game for those who love setting up private servers and the like.

There are only two real negatives I see with the game.
First, because it's now UE5, you get the occasional stutter regardless of system specs.
I'm getting 100fps on Ultra settings with a RTX 4070TI, but even so, I get the stutter.
If I drop it to low settings, I get the occasional stutter.
*I'm not sure how some devs wrestle this issue out of UE5, but hopefully Funcom will get it done.
That said, it's still HIGHLY playable.

The other issue is with the crafting system.
It's a hot mess.  Far too many of the recipes need to be straight remembered.
There's nothing in the game that tells you what makes what for a huge percentage of materials.
I like this mechanic in general.  You have to seek out the secret recipes, but there absolutely needs to be some kind of recipe book that tells you the ones you've learned.
This is compounded by the fact that some recipes are included once you learn them.

Anyway, it's starting to sound like I don't like the game, and I absolutely do not want that to be the message.  I love this game and have been somewhat no-lifing it since getting it.
If Adult Mode Enshrouded sounds cool to you, you will not be disappointed.
Cheers :)

claims.claim: Cooperative multiplayer via Steam forces guests to stay within a restrictive leash distance from the host unless running a dedicated server.

citations.review_text:
We really wanted to like this game but there is one issue : TETHERING DISTANCE.

Got the original game Cheap with some friends and we started to enjoy it, the building - fighting off enemies.  Problem is it was just me and 1 other friend so we didnt notice the tethering as we were always together. Soon as a 3rd and 4th friend joined it was highly noticeable. We were playing from my pc as we do many other Survival games but in Conan if a person goes too far they get pulled back to the main player. This is unacceptable especially in 2026 where Conan has done some major upgrades. The game is old and we all have much newer computers that can handle the distance away from each other.   This is one of the few games that does this.  Even in Ark you can set maximum distance which is entire maps. 

They would have made a lot more money if the distance wasnt so thin as ppl would buy up DLCS. well I am not also paying for a server ontop of it per month which seems to be their shtick money grab. So no DLCS for me, we transferred over to another game Enshrouded which the game is huge and no tethering. 

Fix the tethering issue already

Really cannot recommend.

I bought this game because a friend enjoy the conan universe, so the aim was to play co-op and it really was not as smooth as I would've hoped for compared to most other games out there.

You CAN play co-op via Steam, but the " guest/s " cannot be very far from the " host " due to a leash system. The reason is clearly so the game doesn't have to load too many things at once but man is it outdated.
The only fix for that, as far as i know, is to to setup a dedicated server which could be a problem for some users.
If your objective is to play solo, or multiplayer on a server with PvP in mind, you can ignore these points i guess.

The other thing that i really dislike is the crafting system, everything takes so long by default (you can tinker a bit with the settings). Crafting a big batch of items in certain cases may take a few hours.
I can understand that it's the way it is because of the PvP aspect but when you don't partake in that portion of the game it can become quite frustrating.

And let's not talk about the fact that while there are quite a few DLC (mostly cosmetic to be fair) there is STILL an in-game shop.

There are good things to the game to be honest, i do enjoy the exploration, the combat is alright and some finishers are satisfying, the few dungeons i have done are not bad but i really understand why some players will avoid funcom titles like the plague.

I liked the game to begin with.
I say liked because I won't say love/d.
Conan still has a huge issue where if you're not playing on a dedicated paid server there is a tether between you and ANYONE ELSE that you play with in the game and it HORRIBLY restricts where you can go and how far from your friends (or enemies) you can be.
Unfortunately therefore I will say I can't really recommend it despite this whole Enhanced edition they have offered now. Why wasn't this tethering issue fixed and why would I have to pay for or have an entirely separate tower or server of my own to run a dedicated server over just playing a game with a couple of friends? 
Really really frustrating. If they fix that though then I would say it's fun to go back to once in a while and play with friends. I did own this on PS4 as well back in the day so my metrics are probably skewed as far as playtime and such.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience technical issues and performance drops such as stutters after the Unreal Engine 5 upgrade.

citations.review_text: Conan Exiles Enhanced is a great survival game for players who enjoy exploration, crafting, combat, and building. The Enhanced version gives the game a major visual upgrade through Unreal Engine 5, making the world, characters, armor, buildings, lighting, and environments look much better than before The biggest downside is that Conan Exiles Enhanced still has some technical issues. Players have reported server performance problems, lag, and occasional mod compatibility issues, although Funcom has continued releasing patches and improvements.

Conan Exiles is my favorite survival and craft game, but I cannot recommended it.

It is completely random on whether or not the game will run well, not just between systems, but day to day. Before Enhanced edition it ran at a smooth 90 FPS for me. Afterward, it now runs at 140 fps, but stutters every ten seconds with frame drops all the way down to 32. I've lowered the graphics to their base level, increased shader cache space, and capped the frame rate to no avail. I've tried every tweak under the sun, updated my drivers, and performed numerous restarts and clean installs.

On the last clean install, my controller no longer works. The UI flickers constantly between mouse and keyboard and controller inputs, making both unusable.

You will troubleshoot this game, with zero mods, almost as often as you play it unless you're just very lucky.

An excellent game to start in 2026.  The Enhanced Edition has done wonders for Conan Exiles to make it relevant again.  I had skipped it because, well frankly, by the time I noticed it, it looked far too dated for me.

Now that it has the UE5 treatment (the good and the bad) it's a very viable game in 2026!
If you've played the likes of Valheim or Enshrouded, it's like that but much more mature.
This is not a family game, and I love that about it!

It's also a perfect game for those who love setting up private servers and the like.

There are only two real negatives I see with the game.
First, because it's now UE5, you get the occasional stutter regardless of system specs.
I'm getting 100fps on Ultra settings with a RTX 4070TI, but even so, I get the stutter.
If I drop it to low settings, I get the occasional stutter.
*I'm not sure how some devs wrestle this issue out of UE5, but hopefully Funcom will get it done.
That said, it's still HIGHLY playable.

The other issue is with the crafting system.
It's a hot mess.  Far too many of the recipes need to be straight remembered.
There's nothing in the game that tells you what makes what for a huge percentage of materials.
I like this mechanic in general.  You have to seek out the secret recipes, but there absolutely needs to be some kind of recipe book that tells you the ones you've learned.
This is compounded by the fact that some recipes are included once you learn them.

Anyway, it's starting to sound like I don't like the game, and I absolutely do not want that to be the message.  I love this game and have been somewhat no-lifing it since getting it.
If Adult Mode Enshrouded sounds cool to you, you will not be disappointed.
Cheers :)

claims.claim: The game features a detailed building system that allows players to construct custom fortresses anywhere on a large map.

citations.review_text:
This game is action packed and massive with seemingly endless content, but after all this amount of gameplay and videos I have watched, I always come back to play more of it.  

The Good:  
The building system is simple, yet astounding. You can build anywhere, and it actually looks like a real castle, not just a wooden box.
The thrall (slave lol) system is quite fun. There is nothing quite like knocking out a Tier 4 fighter, putting them on a wheel of pain for 24 hours, and then making them stand guard outside your base.
The map is huge and actually rewards exploration. Dungeons, bosses, and unique recipes are scattered everywhere.

The Bad: 
Buggy as hell. It’s been out for years, and Funcom still manages to break things with every update. Expect clunky AI and the occasional disappearing thralls & pets.
The official PVP servers are toxic dumps. You will get offlined by an alpha clan using exploits while you sleep. Play PVE-Conflict or private servers unless you have a 10-man squad and no job. 
The DLC and Bazaar store prices are getting ridiculous. AND you NEED The Isle of Siptah for achievements, so you must purchase to get 100% completion.

My personal verdict: 
If you like Ark, but prefer slaves in a dark fantasy setting with boobs and gory decapitations, I recommend buying it during a Steam sale.  10/10 would love to get my entire base stomped into absolutely nothing by a frost giant god again for simply existing.

TODAY'S TOPIC: SLAVERY.

This is long, I'M SORRY. Do I recommend? Yes. Do I think it feels unfinished and could use more time in the oven? Also yes.

There is a lot to love here. The building system alone is fantastic. You can make a little survival shack, a sprawling fortress, a gothic castle, or basically whatever architectural fever dream you have in mind. Building our base was one of my favorite parts of the game, and I genuinely never felt like I was running out of things I wanted to add or change.

The thrall system is another huge highlight. There is something incredibly satisfying about capturing an NPC, dragging them back to your base, putting them on the Wheel of Pain, and eventually turning them into a heavily armed employee who will defend your stuff. And once you have the companion system going, the game gets even more fun. Running around with two thralls and casually murdering our way through entire villages was ridiculous in the best possible way. The animals are fun too, although I definitely preferred the human companions. Being able to equip your thralls with actual armor and weapons makes them feel much more useful and customizable. The animals are still great to have around the base, though, and they add some personality to your little house.

The tavern system was probably one of my favorite additions. Watching the base slowly become a place that actually felt lived in was fantastic. Instead of just having a collection of crafting stations and storage boxes, suddenly there were people wandering around, drinking, talking, and generally making the place feel like an actual settlement. It sounds like a small thing, but it made a huge difference.

Exploration is also a lot of fun. The world has a great variety of environments, from deserts and forests to frozen areas and volcanic regions, and there is always something dangerous lurking around the corner. The combat is satisfying, too. You have melee weapons, archery, mounts, sorcery (altho…

Cool mishmash of ideas and gameplay influences that somehow works surprisingly well. The game looks and plays wonderfully, and the world around you is incredibly varied and pleasing to look at. Deserts, tropical areas, snowy peaks, ancient ruins. There are many places and locations to explore, and exploring them is genuinely fun. In one cave you might find a boss, in another a spellbook, and in a third a whole bunch of spiders.
The thrall system is just incredible. Capturing people and then putting them to work gives you a real sense of interacting with your own group or village of inhabitants, much more so than in most other survival games with similar mechanics. Even though the system can sometimes feel a little clunky. You have to place each follower manually, and when moving them you have to carry them one at a time, or two at a time if you have upgraded the relevant skill.
The building system is simply fantastic. It is very simple, while still being varied enough to let you build pretty much any castle or fortress you want, as long as you are willing to grind for the necessary resources.
The magic system is also great. Even at the earliest levels, it provides noticeable and satisfying bonuses, mostly useful for exploration and navigating the world. Creating ice bridges, locating ore, removing fall damage, and so on.
The game does, however, have this slightly unpleasant feeling of an online MMO, early janky survival games, and, strangely enough, Rust. From MMOs it takes grindy progression system, with professions and skills locked behind level caps. It gets almost ridiculous at times. Some regions in the game has its own temperature system, (borrowed from Zelda), and to deal with it you need good armor. Good armor that you have to craft yourself, and you cannot craft necessary equipment until you are approaching level 50, by which point you are already close to the level cap. Leveling up your followers is especially tedious, since they can only gain experience t…

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter difficulties discovering features due to an unhelpful user interface and a lack of clear guidance for crafting recipes and objectives.

citations.review_text:
Mixed feelings.

Some parts of the game are great and feel fresh: the corruption system, capturing thralls, brutality of sacrifices, world design and Conan-themed tone. There's also decent balance between grind and exploration, graphics look nice, music is great.

OTOH many thing comes across like a early access game: large areas of world empty and pointless, poor balancing of encountered enemies, messy and "dead" POIs, incredibly poorly design crafting systems, pointless workstations, unhelpful hints/descriptions of items, lack of proper QoL setup, messy UIs, simplistic building system supporting only most basic building blocks, the fighting system is clunky and frustrating...  After ~50hrs of play I found myself exhausted with trying to like this game :/

Oh, and I need to mention the outrageous DLCs: incredibly expensive cosmetics that the game insists to show off to you each time you expand your character's knowledge... Not cool.

Ui isn't very helpful, needed to do some googling and find theres unlocks to invest points into under another screen when you have a crafting screen on your main tab ui. some kind of highlight or flash would probably help.

claims.claim: Players switching from console or the Microsoft Store to the Steam version are unable to transfer previously purchased DLC and Bazaar content.

citations.review_text:
I cannot recommend Conan Exiles Enhanced because Funcom chose not to honor purchases made through the Microsoft Store version.

I already own the game, roughly $150 worth of DLC, and hundreds of dollars in Bazaar content. To play the Enhanced version on Steam, I would have to buy the game again and lose access to nearly everything I already paid for unless I repurchased it.

Calling this a “free upgrade” is misleading when a portion of the PC player base is effectively being asked to start over and rebuy years of content because Funcom did not provide account linking, entitlement transfer, or even a one-time migration option.

A free Steam key for existing Microsoft Store owners, cross-store DLC recognition, or a one-time Bazaar transfer would have been reasonable. Instead, loyal customers are being punished for purchasing the game on the wrong PC storefront.

I am walking away from Conan Exiles, and I will not purchase another Funcom product. I do not trust the company to respect my purchases.

I have been playing this game since it came out on console (playstation).  I own every DLC, bought and completed all of the battle passes, and purchased about 99% of the bazaar.  I recently made the complete move to pc and currently starting over. (Not being able to transfer purchases from console to pc is a huge suck by the way.  It can be done, and we all know it can so fix that)  This game has had its ups and downs, but continues to hold strong.  Keep giving us content!  great game all around, it has something for everyone.  I would recommend this game to everyone

you guys are sick in the head...i really loved this games had all dlcs on xbox and did buy all on pc again..but now to build a nice yamatai castle i need to pay again for more the tower and stuff in the bazar..thats so ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up...and then you cant even buy it all the times you have to wait for the bazar...no thxs never playing this again..money hungry bastards

Probably one of my favorite games as of lately. Looks amazing while running consistently smooth, Large open world with tons to do and explore, thousands of unique armors and weapons to find/craft, and more freedom than a lot of other sandbox games. The modding scene is also very active and allows a fully custom server. Even after building a large fortress with dozens of NPCs and decorations, I'm still averaging over 60 fps on a dated system and typically getting triple digit fps while exploring.

Only minor complaint is the microtransactions. They aren't as aggressive as other games and to my knowledge are completely cosmetic, but many of the packs offered are dull and forgettable. The bazaar shop is also slightly annoying since its based around a rotating roster of items that can only be obtained through buying an in game currency. It would be nice to have the option to earn these coins outside of paying for them but mods are a very solid substitute to this.

Overall, Highly recommend to solo players and groups.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the deep base-building mechanics and extensive mod support as key features of the game.

citations.review_text: Great game! played it for 351 hours in total, the graphics are great, i love the building mechanic overall i really enjoy this game and i recommend it.

Fantastic game!  Inflexion Studios breathed new life into Conan Exiles.  Game plays well.  Is fun in a social setting.  Am playing on a Private Server.  The Crafting and exploration is very deep.  Two large maps.  Many biomes. Great Dungeons.  Companions.  Pets of all sorts.  It can take hours to get bored.  The Building is very good. The DLC Building sets add a lot of color.  
I bought Conan on sale with all the DLC's a few years ago and sat on it.  After finding my current server, I am completely sold on it.

One of the best modding scenes and RP environments I have seen in decades... The rest is alright, CEE is quite well optimized compared to most UE5 slop we see today.

Bazaar items are way too expensive but that is my only 1 gripe.

Bought it for the survival.

Ended up creating an entire fantasy world.

Conan Exiles gives you an amazing sandbox to play however you want. You can stick to the vanilla survival experience or completely reinvent the game with Steam Workshop mods. Installing mods is incredibly simple, and the community has created thousands of additions ranging from quality-of-life improvements to huge building sets and complete gameplay overhauls.

That's what makes Conan so special to me: it doesn't force you into one playstyle. Want to survive? Go for it. Want to roleplay? Build a kingdom? Create your own world? You can.

It's not a perfect game, but few games have kept me coming back like this one.

This game is outstanding. I recommend it at full price as of July 2026.

I only started playing since the enhanced update, and I'm not sure how this slipped past my radar since 2018. I love survival games like No Man's Sky, Valheim, V Rising, Kenshi, Skyrim, etc., so it's odd this never popped up in my Discovery queue. It "feels" like those other survival games but has character, charm, and brutality of its own. The exploration is filled with wonder and danger, the base building system is great, and I absolutely love the Thrall mechanic.

I waited a bit to review this game; at 100 hours in, I know this one is special. Is it perfect? No, but it's fun as hell, and that's what matters most to me. I wanted to share my thoughts and maybe grab the attention of others like me who might have missed this gem. Take a look if you like those other games I mentioned

Final thoughts:
I only play solo, so I can't speak for online play. The solo options and settings are fantastic and let you customize the game the way you want to play; I love when developers give you the keys to do that. The game runs great on my not-so-current hardware PC. Finally, the Steam Workshop mods are fantastic, current, and add even more flavor to this already amazing game. Give it a try.

citations.review_text: Even in Solo mode, the inventory glitch where your inventory disappears but you remain weighed down, is still a problem. I finally decided to play the game solo to actually beat it this time around. Losing inventory sucks but suppose it is not game breaking. Leaving me weighed down without a way to get rid of the weight however, IS game breaking.  I submitted a ticked a while ago and no response. Devs abandoned this game. DO NOT BUY EVEN ON A DISCOUNT! IT IS A COMPLETE WASTE OF YOUR TIME!

Conan exiles is not a good game anymore, survival/progression feels entirely pointless with how broken thralls are, enemy bodies stretch out or T pose, purges are frequently bugged and dont work properly, you are constantly forced to see an item shop tab when you open your inventory,

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the in-game shop items and bazaar cosmetics are priced too high.

citations.review_text:
One of the best modding scenes and RP environments I have seen in decades... The rest is alright, CEE is quite well optimized compared to most UE5 slop we see today.

Bazaar items are way too expensive but that is my only 1 gripe.

Overall Game: yes worth it

Bazaar: No ( Should of followed in NMS footsteps with free updates, would be way more successful) Cosmetics shouldnt be more than the base game cost..

Gathering, Crafting, Building, Fighting: Good

bosses: Good but needs some balancing. All bosses are easy until you fight the champion where she rips you a new one out of no where.

I love this game... Ive played it a ridiculous amount of hours here as a PVE player... Do I recommend it as a PVE player 100%.  I love the building, the map, and all the animals.  I like the pve community they are very welcoming and helpful to get new players on their feet.  The bazaar items are a little eh since they are kinda pricey but its been fun decorating and exploring and showing off your base to whoever wants to see it.  <---- this is why I personally like the game. 
But I have to give it a BIG THUMBS DOWN for the PvP side... and just to be clear this is just from my experience in the last 3 months of being PvP player.  
There is 100% cheaters in this game. From mesh bases, to esp, body vaulting, exploites, lagswitching, you name it they got it.  The biggest known clans all have a hacker on standby.  If they are getting beaten by players who have learned and adapted to play agasint the cheaters... they all either log and have their hacker come wipe them or they have them come in and wipe the server.  SO MANY PEOPLE LOVE THIS GAME, they just learn to just go to another server and hope for the best.  Its been a learn as you go process but theres so many things overlooked... you can send a video in of a player clearly flying and cheating and lagswitching... they dont get banned.  But you better believe if you say anything that is racial slur or say anything negative about someones mom... be prepared to get banned in less than 24 hours while they let the cheaters stay.  
Its almost accepted in the Conan world of PvP.  At this point in my Conan gamming Imma still try to stick it out with PvP but at the end of the day... PvE is a great fall back and usually stay off the hackers go to list unless they are testing out their hacks before they go to PvP.  So take all that and come play the game lol Ill be the loser still here hoping they will eventually change their allowance of cheaters playing the game

claims.claim: Reviewers report issues connecting to online servers or staying connected without being kicked by Battleye.

citations.review_text:
I WILL NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME IF YOU PLAN ON PLAYING ONLINE PVE OR PVP on official servers. 
This is the worst online gaming experience that iv experienced . Until now i was playing solo and really enjoyed the game despite some shortcomings.
Last month I decided to try the online PVE experience on official servers mainly so the world feels a bit more alive and well i'm in fact pissed. Battleye keeps "kicking me out of the server" at random sometimes every 30 min for no reason. I have a very good internet connexion, i added Battleye to the firewall authorisation , the ping from the online server is 15 , everything should work properly. Well it doesnt, i cannot find a solution online nor does the support has answered me or providing me with any help. 
Obviously you can imagine how frustrating those cuts from Battleye are, even tho i can reconnect immediately , im losing thralls in dungeons; losing unconscious thralls on the rope on my way back to the wheel etc.... 
ON TOP OF IT the lag is AWFUL; i've never seen that before , and I have 1000 hours with Dune Awakening , an other funcom game with battleye. Barely any problem with this game and I play since day one. I leave the comments open in case someone found a solution and experienced this : " BATTLEYE QUERY TIMEOUT"
PS : the cashshop does works without any lag tho , thats for sure.

Spent all this time leveling up and building bases and from one day to the next I can't get into any on line servers. Funcom totally useless in suggesting any way to fix it. Even a complete reinstall didn't help. Deleting...
